::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Is every number compared with infinity virtually zero?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2480837/is-every-number-compared-with-infinity-virtually-zero), asked by [Andres Romero](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/431464/andres-romero) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-10-20; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> When thinking about infinity people think that a great number like googolplex or a googolplexian is closer to infinity, but infinity never ends every huge number that I can think off is closer to zero than to infinity does that make every number virtually zero ?.
:::

Yes.  Every finite number is small compared to $\infty$.  

It's kind of hard to say more without defining “virtually,” but if you give me any positive number $n$ which you might call large, and positive number $\epsilon$ which you might call small, I can find a number $N$ such that $0 < \frac{n}{N} < \epsilon$.  In other words,
$$\lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{n}{x} = 0$$
for any number $n$, no matter how large.
